paragraphs.source_en: How can observers moving at different speeds all measure light at the same speed? The answer is they can't, not if our normal ideas of space and time hold true. However, in a famous paper written in 1905, Einstein pointed out that such observers could ail measure the same speed of light if they abandoned the idea of a universal time. Instead, they would each have their own individual time, as measured by a clock each carried with him. The times measured by these different clocks would agree almost exactly if they were moving slowly with respect to each other - but the times measured by different clocks would differ signifkandy if the clocks were moving at high speed. This effect has actually been observed by comparing a clock on the ground with one in a commercial airliner; the clock in the airliner runs slighdy slow when compared to the stationary clock.
